elements.label: 'Edit' keyboard-shortcut pill with E keycap, rising over the presenter's chest

sfx_review.label: music
sfx_review.note: This is one of a regular series of broadband percussive hits (about 66.38s, 66.6s, 66.88s). It falls about 100 ms before the pill appears, so it reads as a music-bed beat, not an SFX tied to the pill.

sfx_review.label: unsure
sfx_review.note: There is no clear transient at 67.15s on the spectrogram and no visual change in the burst at that moment. The CLAP chime score (0.385) is weak.

pattern.description: A dark rounded pill reading 'Edit' with an 'E' keycap slides up from the bottom of the frame and settles over the presenter's chest just as he says 'Warp now has a code editor'.
pattern.why_premium: A product shortcut hint dropped straight onto live-action footage tells the viewer what the feature is called and how to invoke it, without cutting away from the speaker. The quick rise-and-settle keeps it light and in sync with the narration.

build_hint.gsap: gsap.fromTo(pill, {yPercent: 60, autoAlpha: 0}, {yPercent: 0, autoAlpha: 1, duration: 0.25, ease: 'power3.out'}). If the label and keycap are separate nodes, optionally stagger them by 0.03.
build_hint.remotion: const p = spring({frame: frame - s, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 180, mass: 1}}); translateY = interpolate(p, [0, 1], [40, 0]); opacity = interpolate(p, [0, 0.4], [0, 1], {extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}). Overdamped, no overshoot.

notes: The filmstrip is a crop around the pill. b03 is the OCR box ('Edit. E'); the visible text is 'Edit E'. The full pill extends a bit beyond b03 (about y 500-640 px). b01 and b02 are diff boxes, partly driven by the presenter's mouth moving while he speaks, so they are not listed. Whether there is a fade on top of the slide is uncertain. chip_append was chosen over notification_pop because the pill is a shortcut badge laid onto the footage.
